sources.title: Populating the page: how browsers work
notes: Navigation includes DNS lookup, connection setup, secure negotiation, request and response.
Extra hostnames can require additional DNS lookups, while network latency and bandwidth affect load time.
Parsing, CSS, JavaScript and rendering all influence when content appears and becomes interactive.
sources.apa: MDN Web Docs. (n.d.). Populating the page: how browsers work. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Performance/Guides/How_browsers_work

sources.title: Optimize Largest Contentful Paint
notes: Largest Contentful Paint measures when the main visible content is rendered.
A good LCP target is 2.5 seconds or less for at least 75% of visits.
High time to first byte, redirects, poor networks and render-blocking assets can delay content.
sources.apa: web.dev. (2025). Optimize Largest Contentful Paint. https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp

sources.title: Web performance
notes: Performance includes load time, responsiveness, smooth interactions and perceived speed.
Latency is the time for data to travel between endpoints.
Measure actual user experience as well as lab performance.

sources.title: Lighthouse performance scoring
notes: Lighthouse combines performance metrics into a score; the score is diagnostic, not a complete user-experience description.
Performance metrics have different weights and vary by test conditions.
Use diagnostics to identify bottlenecks rather than optimizing a score in isolation.
sources.apa: Chrome for Developers. (n.d.). Lighthouse performance scoring. https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/performance-scoring

sources.title: Navigation Timing Level 2
notes: Navigation Timing defines browser timestamps for navigation and resource loading milestones.
The measurements help separate DNS, connection, request and response delays.
Timing data helps diagnose where a page load spends time.
sources.apa: World Wide Web Consortium. (n.d.). Navigation Timing Level 2. https://www.w3.org/TR/navigation-timing-2/
